We’re a global close-knit community, united by the relentless pursuit to help keep people safer everywhere. We build and connect technologies to help protect people, property and places. Our solutions foster the collaboration that’s critical for safer communities, safer schools, safer hospitals, safer businesses, and ultimately, safer nations. Connect with a career that matters, and help us build a safer future. Department Overview As a key unit within the Customer Support organization, our team directly supports partners and customers in resolving technical issues with Motorola Solutions' Video Security and Access Control products. We serve as a vital link between frontline support specialists, Product Management, and Engineering to accelerate complex escalations. Our department emphasizes collaborative problem-solving, agent mentorship, and institutional knowledge sharing to build long-term organizational capability. We foster a transparent, customer-first culture that values open communication, teamwork, and continuous career growth. Job Description Technical Support Escalation Point (TSEP) is a senior technical role within the Customer Support organization. The TSEP serves as a high-level technical resource supporting internal stakeholders (Sales, Product, Engineering) and external partners for the Video Security and Access Control portfolio. Technical Swarming: Lead and participate in technical swarms for high-impact or complex cases, establishing clear hypotheses, coordinating troubleshooting actions, and working collaboratively alongside specialists rather than relying on traditional case handoffs. Stakeholder & Engineering Collaboration: Partner closely with Product and Engineering teams to communicate use cases, flag defects, construct reproducible problem statements, validate fixes or workarounds, and drive product quality improvements. Mentorship & Upskilling: Provide real-time coaching and mentorship to Support Specialists during technical investigations, sharing troubleshooting best practices and product knowledge to build overall team capability. Knowledge Management: Act as a Knowledge Centered Service (KCS) Champion by converting escalation findings into concise case notes, reusable troubleshooting documentation, known-issue articles, and internal Knowledge Base content. Case & Investigation Guidance: Review complex or stalled cases to identify paths forward, ensure proper diagnostic evidence is collected prior to further escalation, and guide specialists while preserving case ownership with the assigned agent. Problem & Trend Identification: Analyze technical issue trends and escalation patterns to surface recurring defects or systemic problems, leading workflow optimization projects to improve support efficiency. Technical Proficiency: Maintain deep technical expertise across IP networking (RTP, TCP/IP, IGMP), operating systems, and diagnostic tools such as Wireshark, PowerShell, Dell iDRAC, and HP iLO. Bachelor's Degree or Diploma/Certificate in Computer Science, Engineering, or a relevant software/computer-related field. Technical Expertise & Tooling: Deep understanding of IP networking integrations (RTP, TCP/IP, IGMP), VMS (Video Management Systems), scripting, and diagnostic tools (Wireshark, PowerShell, Dell iDRAC, HP iLO); relevant certifications (CCNA, CCNP, CompTIA A+, etc.) are highly valued. Communication & Mentorship: Exceptional written and verbal communication skills with the proven ability to translate complex technical concepts for diverse audiences, coach support agents, and author technical documentation. Operational Requirements: Ability to work in a hybrid office environment (twice per week) and handle weekend on-call shifts as required. With 64 television stations in 51 U.S. markets, TEGNA reaches more than 100 million people monthly across the web, mobile apps, streaming, and linear television. Together, we are building a sustainable future for local news. This Operations Analyst role is part of a team that owns the day-to-day monitoring, support, and operational stability of TEGNA's broadcast and digital platforms while providing advanced support to stakeholders and business-critical applications. You'll work closely with distributed IT teams, engineering, and vendors in a 24x7 support environment—triaging incidents, resolving tickets, and keeping services online. Automating the repetitive task with AI and workflow tools. You'll leverage intelligent ticket routing, help implement our next predictive monitoring solution, and automations. Clear ownership from intake through resolution, sharp communication, and the ability to work across technical teams. Incident Support & Workflow Automation Own support tickets in ServiceNow from intake through resolution, with responsibility for issues spanning PC/Mac endpoints, imaging workflows, collaborative tools (Teams/O365), and emerging AI/workstream tooling. Troubleshoot complex endpoint issues across Intune (device compliance, conditional access, app distribution), hybrid identity systems (Okta, AD, Entra), and Exchange Online. Leverage Moveworks for intelligent ticket intake, prioritization, and automated routing to reduce manual triage. Coordinate cross-functionally with remote teams, document root causes and remediation steps in ServiceNow, and drive first-contact resolution rates. Identify automation opportunities—flagging repetitive tickets for workflow automation, knowledge gaps, and tooling inefficiencies that slow resolution. The role is also responsible for monitoring and supporting patch compliance. System Monitoring and Operational Support Provide proactive monitoring and day-to-day operational support for critical broadcast and streaming systems by responding to PagerDuty alerts, performing routine health checks in New Relic and native monitoring platforms, identifying early warning indicators, and taking preventative action to avoid service disruption. Own operational dashboards and alert tuning to reduce noise and catch real issues early. Problem Management and Documentation Analyze, resolve, and document incidents and recurring problems using structured root cause analysis. Capture resolutions, workarounds, and lessons learned in ServiceNow knowledge articles and operational runbooks. Drive continuous refinement of documentation to reduce repeat tickets and improve first-contact resolution rates. Knowledge Management and Operational Readiness Create, maintain, and improve operational documentation, standard operating procedures, and knowledge base content to support the Service Desk and enable effective remote handoffs across distributed teams. Build self-service resources that reduce support load and empower end users. Operational Flexibility and Continuous Improvement Adapt to changing priorities and operational demands, take ownership of assigned work, and constructively challenge existing tools and processes. Identify automation opportunities and champion process improvements that increase reliability, efficiency, and support outcomes. Team Collaboration and Remote Support Collaborate effectively with a globally distributed, remote-first team, including engineers, application owners, and broadcast/streaming operations. Support handoffs across time zones and enable a follow-the-sun operating model with clear communication and documentation. Requirements College degree, relevant certifications, or equivalent hands-on experience in IT operations, service desk, or enterprise support roles. Three or more years of experience in an operations or advanced helpdesk role, supporting enterprise applications, infrastructure, and end-user environments in a production or 24x7 support setting. Demonstrated experience supporting broadcast, media, or digital workflow systems, including server platforms, end-user computing orchestration, and monitoring/management toolsets. Cloud and hybrid environment experience is a plus. Strong working knowledge of IT service management practices and tooling, including ITIL concepts, incident and problem management, knowledge management, and ServiceNow. Hands-on experience with automation and scripting technologies, such as PowerShell, Python, or similar languages, used to improve operational efficiency and reduce manual support effort. Proven ability to manage and prioritize multiple concurrent tickets, incidents, or tasks, working independently while collaborating effectively with remote and globally distributed teams. Effective written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to clearly document issues and resolutions and communicate technical information to a wide range of internal customers and business partners. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to troubleshoot complex technical issues and identify practical, repeatable solutions. Benefits TEGNA offers comprehensive benefits designed to safeguard the physical, mental and financial health of our employees and their families. TEGNA offers two medical plan options for full and part-time employees through Blue Cross Blue Shield of Texas, as well as access to dental and eye care coverage; fertility, surrogacy and adoption assistance; disability and life insurance. Our 401(k) program offers full, part-time and temporary employees the opportunity to contribute 1% - 80% of their pay on a pre-tax basis to TEGNA’s 401(k). Contributions made up to the first 4% of pay are eligible for a 100% match from the company and are 100% vested from day one. Regardless of participation in TEGNA medical plans, ALL employees and their eligible family members receive nine free virtual doctor’s appointments with a physician through Teladoc, and 12 free annual therapy sessions with a licensed clinician through Spring Health. TEGNA offers a generous Paid Time Off (PTO) benefit as well as nine paid holidays per year. Some jobs are covered by a collective bargaining agreement and thus some or all of the benefits described herein may not apply. For example, some newsroom bargaining unit employees receive health and retirement benefits under plans administered by the union. EEO Statement TEGNA Inc. is a proud equal opportunity employer. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer, hiring and developing individuals from diverse backgrounds and experiences to add to our collaborative culture. We value and consider applications from all qualified candidates without regard to actual or perceived race, color, religion, national origin, sex, gender, age, marital status, personal appearance, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, family responsibilities, disability, medical condition, enrollment in college or vocational school, political affiliation, military or veteran status, citizenship status, genetic information, or any other basis protected by federal, state or local law. TEGNA will reasonably accommodate qualified individuals with disabilities in accordance with applicable law. If you are in need of an accommodation in order to submit your application, please email askhr@tegna.com Recruiting Fraud Alert To all candidates: your personal information and online safety are important to us. Only TEGNA Recruiters or Hiring Managers will reach out to you regarding consideration of your application or background. Communications with TEGNA employees will either come from a TEGNA email address with a domain of tegna.com or one of our affiliate station domains. Recruiters or Hiring Managers will never request payments, ask for financial account information or sensitive information such as social security numbers. review_candidates.title: Head Of Business Operations
review_candidates.description: Glassworks London is an independent fashion retail and ecommerce business founded in London in 2010. We operate across retail stores, ecommerce, warehouse fulfilment, product, marketing, brand, finance, HR, international production and distributed teams. We are building a more scalable, systems-led business with stronger operating rhythm, clearer accountability and less founder dependency. THE ROLE The Head of Business Operations is the senior operating-system role at Glassworks. This person makes sure the company runs as one coherent business: priorities are clear, owners are accountable, KPIs are reviewed, actions close, issues are escalated properly, operating standards stay live and work does not stall simply because Founder review has not happened. The Head of Business Operations is responsible for ensuring that work does not stop merely because the Founder has not reviewed it. Functional owners must have sufficient standards, decision rights, escalation routes and operating infrastructure to continue execution wherever reasonably possible. This is not a founder PA, project coordinator, warehouse manager, general fixer, or software architect. It is a senior business operations role for someone who can manage managers, improve systems, diagnose operating failures, drive recovery and build organisational capability. REPORTING LINES Reports to: Founder / CEO Direct reports: HR Operations Lead, Operations & Facilities Manager, Order Fulfilment & Warehouse Manager Business Systems & Technology Operations is a critical functional partnership. The role will begin with a deliberately focused direct-report mandate and is expected to take on broader operating responsibility as capability and organisational readiness are demonstrated. WORKING PATTERN / LOCATION Remote / offshore role working UK business hours, Monday to Friday, 9am to 5.30pm UK time. The successful candidate must be able to operate fully within the UK working day and lead across a distributed company, including UK, USA, Korea, India and external suppliers. Key Responsibilities Own the company operating rhythm, including weekly cadence, action registers, decision logs, cross-functional follow-up and escalation. Create and maintain a concise recurring operating report / management pack for the Founder / CEO, covering key operational KPIs, actual vs target, material variances, root cause, accountable owner, corrective action, deadline, recovery status, blockers and decisions required. Ensure reporting drives action. Where KPIs are off track, the Head of Business Operations must ensure an appropriate recovery plan exists and is being driven by the responsible functional owner. Ensure major operational functions define appropriate KPIs, report them accurately, review them at the correct cadence, investigate misses, create corrective actions and recover performance. Drive action and commitment closure: what is due, who owns it, what evidence exists, what is drifting and what intervention has happened. Hold functional owners accountable across Retail, Ecommerce, Warehouse, HR Operations, Finance, Creative / Brand, Marketing, Buying, Merchandising, Production, Business Development and external partners. Diagnose operating failures, including whether the issue is infrastructure, ownership, capacity, role capability, management behaviour, process, systems, training or performance. Apply Build / QA / Own discipline, ensuring recurring work has a clear operating rail, QA gate, owner, evidence standard and review rhythm. Own organisational capacity and productivity, including under-used roles, overloaded roles, duplicated work, founder-held work and unclear responsibilities. Own business continuity when people leave, roles change, responsibilities are exposed or recurring work becomes unowned. Own the inventory-accuracy management rhythm, including the company-level operating system required to improve and sustain stock accuracy across warehouse, stores, transfers, locations, discrepancies, stocktakes and process compliance. Understand and challenge inventory controls, including location accuracy, receiving, put-away, transfers, stocktakes, cycle counts, discrepancy resolution, faulty-stock treatment, system controls, process controls and WMS / inventory-system requirements. Provide operational assurance across ecommerce fulfilment, warehouse operations and retail operating dependencies, without becoming the warehouse manager or retail manager. Own HR Operations rhythm, including recruitment administration, onboarding, offboarding, probation control, people-process follow-through and manager HR actions. Own SOP and operating-standard governance, ensuring critical processes are documented, current, trained, used and reviewed. Own technology priorities from an operating / business perspective, ensuring material technology gaps are surfaced, implementations have clear business owners and adoption expectations, and systems blocking company performance are escalated. Partner with Business Systems & Technology Operations on requirements translation, solution/vendor evaluation, configuration, technical implementation, integrations, migration, UAT, rollout, system documentation and access / permissions infrastructure. Ensure the company has an effective IT / technology-support operating model across UK and international teams, including appropriate support routes, escalation of unresolved technology problems, joiner/leaver access, and visibility of hardware, software and access dependencies. Drive recovery when plans fail, including evidence review, reset plans, owner accountability, escalation and follow-through. What We�re Looking For We are looking for evidence of: senior business operations, operating-system leadership or operations integration experience; meaningful experience in fast-moving omnichannel retail, ecommerce, consumer, grocery or comparable multi-site operations; management of managers or credible authority across experienced functional owners; building operating cadence across multiple teams or functions; creating KPI rhythms that improve outcomes, not just reporting activity; preparing useful CEO / senior-management reporting that leads to decisions and recovery action; closing cross-functional issues with owner / action / deadline / evidence discipline; reducing founder, CEO or senior-leader dependency; diagnosing infrastructure, capability, ownership, process, systems, capacity and performance problems; sufficient inventory-management fluency to understand and challenge inventory accuracy, receiving, put-away, stocktakes, transfers, discrepancies, faulty stock and inventory-system controls; improving operational outcomes through systems, dashboards, automation, AI, SOPs or workflow redesign; commercial understanding across stock, stores, customers, fulfilment, cost, service and operational risk; distributed-team leadership and the ability to know what is really happening without being physically present. You should be structured without being bureaucratic, commercially literate, systems-minded, AI-capable, calm under pressure, direct with managers and able to escalate with options and recommendations. What Success Looks Like Strong performance will be visible when: the Founder is no longer the default chaser of routine operational actions; functional owners know what they own, what is due and what evidence is required; CEO / Founder reporting gives clear visibility of KPIs, variances, root causes, owners, corrective actions and decisions required; work continues where reasonably possible without waiting for founder review; repeated drift is diagnosed early and moved into recovery plans; managers are challenged before problems are escalated upward; major operational KPIs are reviewed accurately and drive corrective action; inventory accuracy improves through better rhythm, standards, evidence and accountability; warehouse, ecommerce fulfilment and retail operating dependencies are visible and controlled; HR Ops works inside a clear service and priority rhythm; Business Systems & Technology Operations work is prioritised against real operating needs; IT and technology-support issues have clear routes, owners and escalation rather than drifting unresolved; SOPs, training and operating standards stay current and used; absences, resignations and role gaps create continuity plans rather than organisational fog. ROLE BOUNDARIES This Role Does Not Own founder strategy; product / buying judgement; creative or brand judgement; marketing strategy; final Finance judgement; HR/legal specialist judgement; software architecture or technical implementation; system configuration, integrations, migration or access / permissions infrastructure; personal administration for the Founder; personally performing warehouse / stock-control work; day-to-day warehouse management; retail trading; rescuing unfinished work from functional owners indefinitely. The role owns the operating rhythm, infrastructure, accountability, KPI challenge, recovery and closure around functions, not every specialist decision or task inside them.
